newsitem.title: FRANCE: DGAC maintains some cargo flights for first time.
newsitem.headline: DGAC maintains some cargo flights for first time.

text.p: France's civil aviation authority, the DGAC, said it had maintained some all-cargo flights in a minimum service flight programme for the first time.

Flights to and from French airports will be reduced to around 15 percent its normal volume from 0500 gmt, on October 17 to 0500 gmt, October 18 as a result of a strike by public sector workers which is being supported by air traffic controllers.
Surveillance of aircraft overflying of French airspace will be assured as normal, the DGAC added.

"Maintaining some all-cargo flights tomorrow and in particular, those of freight express carriers, is recognition that a 24-hour cancellation can have very serious consequences on their operations," a DGAC official told Reuters.
Full details on the all-cargo flights cancelled and those maintained were not available at this stage, the official said.

Among the flights scheduled to operate as normal are Federal Express' McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter services between Paris and the U.S. and Korean Airlines' Boeing 747-400F service between Paris and Seoul, which is run in partnership with Air France. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
